newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Russia, Central Asian states to meet on Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Central Asian states to meet on Afghanistan.

text.p: Foreign ministers of the Central Asian states and Russia will meet in the Tajik capital Dushanbe on Saturday to hold consultations over the situation in the region bordering war-torn Afghanistan.
Igor Sattarov, head of the information department at the Tajik Foreign Ministry, told Reuters by telephone from Dushanbe on Thursday that the main topic would be bilateral realtions.
But a diplomat working in Dushanbe and who requested anonymity told Reuters: "The Afghan issue is likely to dominate the discussions."

Former Soviet republics of Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Russia have already confirmed their participation in the consultations, Sattarov said, adding it was unclear if Turkmenistan would be represented as well.
Russia may be represented by a deputy foreign minister.

The Central Asian states and Russia have repeatedly voiced their concern about a possible advance of militant Islam from nearby Afghanistan where the Taleban -- the purist Moslem militia -- controls three quarters of the territory.
Russia keeps a military contingent of some 20,000 peacekeepers and border guards in Tajikistan.
